title: Search the shelf
concept: Searching · one item at a time
description: The archive keeps records on long shelves. Search them one by one, and count how many you had to look at.

tasks.title: Look at each item until you find it
tasks.body: A linear search checks the items in order, from the first, until it finds the one it wants or runs out. It works on any list, sorted or not.
tasks.detail: Counting how many items it looks at, its steps, tells you how much work it did. Found at the start: 1 step. Found at the end, or not there at all: as many steps as there are items. Doubling the list doubles the worst case.

tasks.code:
# Look along the shelf, one box at a time
shelf = ["rope", "map", "lamp", "key"]
looks = 0
found_at = -1
for i in range(len(shelf)):
    looks = looks + 1
    if shelf[i] == "lamp":
        found_at = i
        break
print(found_at, looks)
tasks.note: lamp is at position 2, and finding it took 3 looks: rope, map, lamp. break stops the loop as soon as it is found.

tasks.question: If the shelf held 1,000 boxes and the one wanted was not there, how many looks would it take?
tasks.why: To be sure something is missing, a linear search has to look at every item.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: search for "key", then for "sword", which is not there, and compare the counts.

Write find(items, target), which looks through the list items from the start.

1. Return a list of two numbers: the position of the first item equal to target, and how many items it looked at to get there.
2. If target is not there, return -1 and the number of items it looked at, which is all of them.

Do not ask for input: the check calls your functions with its own values.
hints: Keep a count of looks that starts at 0, and go through the positions in order, adding one each time you look at an item.
As soon as an item matches, return its position and the count, together. If the loop ends, nothing matched: return -1 and the count after the loop.
With other names: for spot in range(len(row)): with tries = tries + 1 inside, and return [spot, tries] when row[spot] == wanted.

error_hints.text: Use the parameter names from the def line, spelled the same way.
A position is past the end: range(len(items)) gives exactly the positions there are.
find(["rope", "map", "lamp", "key"], "lamp") should return [2, 3]: position 2, after looking at 3 items.
When target is not there, return -1 and the number of items looked at: all of them.
Check a list where the target is the first item: one look.
Check a list with the target in it twice: the first one counts.

similar_example.note: A linear search for the first even number, counting looks. Yours returns a position, not the item.

other_ways.note: enumerate() numbers the items as it goes, here from 1, so the count and the position come together.
A while loop that stops at a match or at the end. The number of looks follows from where it stopped.

cases.description: a target that is there twice
